lead: reversible super-reduction with downstream kinetic commitment in cyclopropyl-ketone/styrene annulation
overall_status: The source-reported chemistry is a distinct mechanism line. A conditional multichannel static design theorem and exact checker are internally reconstructed and finite-tested. No in-situ chemical capability, external validation, priority, or novelty claim is established.

claims.exact_statement_assumptions: Edgecomb et al. report formal [3+2] annulation between the more difficult-to-reduce cyclopropyl ketone Ket-1 and easier-to-reduce styrene using perylene electrophotocatalysis, with 70% annulation product A and 7% styrene-hydrogenation product B in the 390-nm screen despite an approximately 1-V redox mismatch. This is the source's reported outcome and mechanistic interpretation, not an independent replication.
claims.proof_path: SOURCE_NOTES.md; official Nature abstract and official SI S7-S13, S25-S30, S81-S86
claims.novelty_boundary: The two-channel selectivity mechanism is stated and modeled in the source. The formal transformation and broad super-reduction/BET ideas predate it. No priority claim is made.
claims.costs: 0.3 mmol substrate charge; about 0.075 M; 7.5 mol% perylene; 390-nm Kessil; 1-mA electrolysis to roughly 1 F/mol; about 7.75 h; divided cell; Zn sacrificial anode; RVC cathode; 0.4-M electrolytes; DMF; nitrogen; extraction and silica chromatography. Cell-voltage integral, lamp wall power, absorbed photon count, quantum yield, and energy per product are unreported.
claims.falsifier: A same-condition independent experiment fails to reproduce the product split or shows the purported ketone-fragmentation/BET competition is absent.
claims.next_gate: Resolve the SI Ket-1 SET-rate conflict and acquire full channel-specific rates in the operating reaction mixture.

claims.exact_statement_assumptions: The official SI S2.18 plot label and SI S30 prose give Ket-1 solvated-electron capture kET=4e9 M^-1 s^-1; the S2.18 figure caption instead gives 3e10, equal to the styrene value in S2.3. The SI S2.18 caption also calls the capture 'by pyrene' though the experiment is headed Ket-1 as quencher. Preserve g=2/15 and g=1 as competing source readings at equal substrate concentration; neither is silently chosen as a corrected fact.
claims.proof_path: SOURCE_NOTES.md; official SI S73 Figure S2.18 and SI S25/S30; candidate_scan/GATE_DERIVATION.md
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a source-data inconsistency, not a new chemical result.
claims.costs: A resolved value requires same-solvent, same-mixture transient-quenching acquisition for both substrates and uncertainty reporting.
claims.falsifier: An author correction or replicated source dataset establishes a single consistent Ket-1 rate and identifies the erroneous SI occurrence.
claims.next_gate: Re-measure both capture constants under operating conditions.

claims.exact_statement_assumptions: For independent two-channel reduced intermediates generated at alpha_i D with constant concentrations, product hazard c_i and BET hazard b_i A, quasi-steady state gives v_1/v_2=(alpha_1/alpha_2)*(c_1/c_2)*(c_2+b_2 A)/(c_1+b_1 A). This is algebraically equivalent to the source's SI Eq. S9 after alpha_i=kET_i[S_i].
claims.novelty_boundary: Not novel; the source prints the equivalent two-channel relation as Eq. S9.
claims.costs: Requires acquired forward-capture, BET, commitment, and concentration values; ignores depletion, cross-channel pathways, and optical/electrical conversion.
claims.falsifier: The measured branch fluxes disagree with the identity after the declared independent-channel/QSS interface is verified; that would reject the model interface rather than the algebra.
claims.next_gate: Validate the per-channel hazard model on time-resolved products.

claims.exact_statement_assumptions: For m independent QSS channels with v_i=D*alpha_i*q_i/(q_i+A), q_i=c_i/b_i, a target j whose q_j is at least every competing q_i has nondecreasing target product share in A and high-A limiting share alpha_j q_j/sum_i(alpha_i q_i).
claims.novelty_boundary: Internal extension of source-reported two-channel kinetic partitioning; mathematical and literature novelty are UNKNOWN.
claims.costs: Needs each channel's effective first-passage commitment hazard c_i and BET coefficient b_i, acquired under the actual reaction mixture.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample satisfying positive independent-channel/QSS assumptions violates monotonicity; the derivative proof currently rules this out.
claims.next_gate: Prior-art search and physical parameter acquisition for at least three competing product channels.

claims.exact_statement_assumptions: Under independent rectangular intervals for alpha_i and q_i=c_i/b_i, if the target lower q endpoint is at least every side channel's upper q endpoint, the target-share lower envelope is monotone. Exact rational bisection certifies a minimum acceptor setpoint meeting a selectivity floor or returns REFUTED/UNKNOWN; with a finite pool D+A=C_T, target throughput is maximal at the smallest feasible A.
claims.novelty_boundary: Novelty and practical usefulness are UNKNOWN; generic robust control and kinetic branching prior art remain to be compared.
claims.costs: One exact interval acquisition per channel, measured pool size, operating A setpoint, electron-transfer-attempt count proxy, plus actual photon and cell-energy measurement. The script's exact witness parameters are constructed, not measured.
claims.falsifier: A held-out target fraction lies below the certified interval bound under a verified interface, or the calibrated intervals fail to contain a real channel rate.
claims.next_gate: Resolve the source conflict, obtain actual chemistry intervals, and compare a held-out design with matched-information redox-potential control.

claims.exact_statement_assumptions: For equal capture ratio g=2/15 and common BET, the high-BET limit requires q_target/q_easy>=67.5 for a 90% target share and >=75 for 10:1 product odds. At the SI's illustrative beta=560, the finite-BET k_target/k_easy thresholds are 3600/47 for 90% and 7000/81 for 10:1. Under caption-literal g=1, the corresponding finite gates are 210/23 and 5600/551. These are exact model thresholds, not measured Ket-1 commitment rates or predictions of the source endpoint.
claims.novelty_boundary: Arithmetic applied to a source-known two-channel mechanism; no claim of novelty.
claims.costs: The q/beta values required to convert thresholds to an experiment must be measured; electron-attempt counts are not photons, current, yield, or energy.
claims.falsifier: The exact script or algebra fails its rational checks; physical applicability is falsified by same-condition data outside the resulting valid-model prediction interval.
claims.next_gate: Acquire in-situ alpha, commitment, BET, [A], photons, and charge.

claims.exact_statement_assumptions: The multichannel interval theorem predicts an experimentally useful optimum for any real photoredox/electrochemical reaction, including Ket-1/styrene, with finite resource accounting.
claims.novelty_boundary: No priority claim; exact two-channel source result is published, and multi-channel resource-aware novelty is unreviewed.
claims.costs: No full photon, wall-plug, cell-voltage, absorbed energy, or product-workup cost was obtained in this audit.
claims.falsifier: Same-condition kinetic rates violate the channel model, predicted held-out split falls outside the interval, or a matched-information/matched-cost Marcus baseline dominates the selectivity-throughput-energy point.
claims.next_gate: Run the decisive same-condition calibration and held-out reaction test listed in FINAL_REPORT.md.
